data.title: MFA Method Switch Before High-Value Transaction
data.description: Detects when an account's multi-factor authentication method is changed (e.g., from hardware token to SMS or email OTP) shortly before a high-value wire or ACH transaction is initiated. Attackers downgrade MFA to a method they control prior to executing fraud.

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for MFA Method Switch Before High-Value Transaction")`
`comment("Aggregation that cannot be expressed in Sigma")`
`comment("Original condition: selection_mfa_change | near selection_high_value_txn by account_id")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:identity_management
event_type="MFA_METHOD_CHANGE"
(new_mfa_method="sms_otp" OR new_mfa_method="email_otp" OR new_mfa_method="voice_call")
(event_type="WIRE_INITIATION" OR event_type="ACH_DEBIT")
transaction_amount>=5000
| transaction account_id maxspan=4h
| where eventcount >= 2

falsepositives: Customer who lost their hardware token and is making a legitimate scheduled payment
Planned MFA migration events by IT or security teams
